sentences.text: Armadillosuchus was a large and robust sphagesaurid crocodylomorph, considered one of the best-armored notosuchians due to its distinctive body armor.
The animal possessed a robust, slightly flattened skull and a prominent body armor made of small bony plates called osteoderms.

The holotype specimen UFRJ DG 303-R is a well-preserved partial skeleton including the entire skull, neck, cervical osteoderms, front torso, and a nearly complete left forelimb, while a second paratype consists of partial upper and lower jaws.
The back was covered by armor with flexible bands and rigid protectors similar to an armadillo, reflecting the genus name meaning "armadillo crocodile".
Armadillosuchus possessed heterodont teeth that gave it powerful, scissor-like jaws capable of chewing its food.
Unlike modern crocodilians, Sharpey's fibers ran perpendicular to the outer surface of the osteoderms, suggesting they were deeply embedded in the skin and covered by a leathery dermis.
This deep embedding likely provided the animal with increased flexibility and may have helped absorb and retain heat during basking.
The genus Armadillosuchus was described by Marinho and Carvalho in 2009, with the type species Armadillosuchus arrudai named from fossils found in the Upper Cretaceous Bauru Basin in Brazil.
The species name arrudai honors João Tadeu Arruda for his contributions to the paleontology of the region.

Based on its teeth and size, Armadillosuchus is believed to have been an omnivore that ate invertebrates, plants, and possibly scavenged. Wear facets on the teeth suggest the animal used a back-and-forth chewing motion, and it is possible the animal occasionally scavenged dried carcasses, which may have caused the observed tooth wear.
The animal may have used gastroliths to assist in grinding food alongside its specialized teeth.

Researchers suggest that Armadillosuchus's well-developed forelimbs may have allowed it to burrow, potentially helping it regulate its body temperature, and due to its singular morphology, it is believed to have had a subterranean lifestyle.
The reconstruction of the armor on the back of the body remains difficult due to only isolated material being known.
The animal lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.

In a 2026 review, Kitayama and Bertini provisionally proposed that Armadillosuchus arrudai is a junior synonym of Sphagesaurus huenei. Kitayama and Bertini argued that the features distinguishing Armadillosuchus arrudai were insufficiently diagnostic and might represent intraspecific variation or deformation. The proposal to synonymize Armadillosuchus arrudai with Sphagesaurus huenei remains provisional and could change with new specimens or analyses.
It is debated whether terrestrial Notosuchians like Armadillosuchus regulated temperature like modern monitor lizards rather than like modern crocodilians.
